fieldHelp.description: How to fill out this field accurately.

accountName.title: Account or wallet name
accountName.meaning: Name the actual place that holds money or debt, not the purpose of your budget. A food budget can be spread across several accounts.
accountName.example: Use BCA, DANA, and Cash as separate accounts, then classify food purchases under the Food category.
accountName.important: Avoid adding the same real balance twice. Click the square logo tile to choose a brand, monogram, or icon.

accountCurrency.title: Account currency
accountCurrency.meaning: Choose the actual currency held, such as IDR for a Rupiah bank account or wallet.
accountCurrency.example: BCA Rp1,250,000 uses IDR; a separate USD account should use USD.
accountCurrency.important: The account currency cannot be edited after creation in the current application.

accountInitialBalance.title: Choosing your opening balance
accountInitialBalance.meaning: The balance before your first recorded transaction, not always today's balance if you plan to backfill earlier transactions.
accountInitialBalance.example: If today's balance is 1,000,000 and you will record a past expense of 150,000, begin with 1,150,000 to end at today's balance.
accountInitialBalance.important: Imports may adjust the opening balance. Do not double-count initial money as income.

accountCategory.title: Account category vs. spending category
accountCategory.meaning: Account category mainly changes the account's label and icon; it does not allocate money to a budget purpose or create an investment portfolio.
accountCategory.example: Cash wallet → Cash, BCA savings → Savings account. There is no dedicated e-wallet enum yet; use General with a clear name temporarily.
accountCategory.important: Credit card category can affect the classification of liabilities in net-worth reports.

accountPaymentType.title: Default payment method
accountPaymentType.meaning: This preselects how a transaction was paid, not which account holds the funds. Leave it as None if no method applies consistently.
accountPaymentType.example: A QR payment using BCA has account BCA and a digital payment method; a bank transfer is not cash.
accountPaymentType.important: You can change the method per transaction. A single bank account can support several methods.

accountCreditLimit.title: Credit limit and debt
accountCreditLimit.meaning: Credit limit is the amount a lender authorizes for a card or overdraft. It is not cash, income, or your spending budget.
accountCreditLimit.example: Limit 10,000,000, spent 2,000,000: outstanding debt is 2,000,000, with 8,000,000 of limit remaining.
accountCreditLimit.important: Beware the Include credit limits in balance setting: subtracting the limit from an already negative card balance can double-count debt.

vehicleName.title: Vehicle name
vehicleName.meaning: A vehicle is a noncash asset whose estimated value changes over time. The name is for recognizing it in your records.
vehicleName.example: Daily Vario, Family Avanza, or Office Beat.
vehicleName.important: Avoid recording the same vehicle value as both a cash account and a vehicle asset.

vehicleCurrency.title: Vehicle currency
vehicleCurrency.meaning: Use the currency of the vehicle's purchase price and ongoing valuation.
vehicleCurrency.example: An Indonesian motorcycle purchased for Rp26,000,000 uses IDR.
vehicleCurrency.important: The currency cannot be changed after vehicle creation.

vehicleMake.title: Vehicle make
vehicleMake.meaning: The manufacturer's brand, rather than the model or trim.
vehicleMake.example: Toyota, Daihatsu, Honda, Yamaha, Suzuki, or Wuling.
vehicleMake.important: Make alone does not fetch Indonesian resale prices.

vehicleModel.title: Vehicle model
vehicleModel.meaning: The product family under a brand, distinct from the year or trim.
vehicleModel.example: Toyota Avanza, Honda Vario, Daihatsu Xenia.
vehicleModel.important: The model name is currently informational and does not determine depreciation.

vehicleTrim.title: Vehicle trim / variant
vehicleTrim.meaning: An optional specific edition with transmission, engine, or feature details.
vehicleTrim.example: Avanza G CVT, Brio Satya E, Vario 160 CBS.
vehicleTrim.important: Trim does not currently adjust the vehicle's calculated value.

vehicleYear.title: Model or manufacturing year
vehicleYear.meaning: Use the vehicle model/manufacturing year, not when you personally bought it.
vehicleYear.example: A 2021 Brio bought second-hand in 2026 has Year 2021 and Purchase date 2026.
vehicleYear.important: The app's depreciation curve starts from your purchase date, even for used vehicles.

vehicleClass.title: Vehicle class and limitations
vehicleClass.meaning: The class drives the depreciation formula. Current classes mix body style, prestige, and powertrain, rather than a consistent Indonesian taxonomy.
vehicleClass.example: Vario → Motorcycle; Fortuner → SUV; MPV such as Avanza has no dedicated option, so Other is only a provisional choice.
vehicleClass.important: The curves have not been calibrated to Indonesian resale data. Electric and Luxury are not mutually exclusive with body style.

vehiclePurchasePrice.title: Vehicle purchase price
vehiclePurchasePrice.meaning: Enter the actual acquisition price, used as the initial valuation anchor.
vehiclePurchasePrice.example: A motorcycle bought for 28,000,000 is entered as 28,000,000; record financing debt separately.
vehiclePurchasePrice.important: Purchase price cannot be edited after creating the vehicle in the current app.

vehiclePurchaseDate.title: Vehicle purchase date
vehiclePurchaseDate.meaning: The date you acquired the vehicle, not the model year or first loan installment.
vehiclePurchaseDate.example: A used 2020 Avanza purchased on 10 Nov 2026 has purchase date 10 Nov 2026.
vehiclePurchaseDate.important: Purchase date cannot be edited after creation; it anchors the depreciation timeline.

vehicleDepreciation.title: Depreciation pattern
vehicleDepreciation.meaning: Class default uses a yearly value-loss curve; Slow is 30% lower rates, Fast 30% higher, and Custom applies a single annual rate.
vehicleDepreciation.example: For a sample sedan purchased for 200,000,000: first-year value 160,000,000, second-year value 136,000,000 under the existing formula.
vehicleDepreciation.important: These curves rely on foreign-market assumptions; condition, mileage and Indonesian resale market prices are not modeled.

vehicleCustomRate.title: Custom yearly depreciation
vehicleCustomRate.meaning: Percentage deducted from the remaining value each year, not a fixed nominal reduction.
vehicleCustomRate.example: At 10% annual loss, a 100,000,000 value becomes 90,000,000 after one year and 81,000,000 after two.
vehicleCustomRate.important: A user-chosen rate is an assumption, not an official resale valuation.

vehicleFloor.title: Minimum residual value
vehicleFloor.meaning: The mathematical minimum floor for the depreciation calculation, expressed as a share of the purchase price or latest override.
vehicleFloor.example: With a purchase of 100,000,000 and floor 10%, the projection will not drop below 10,000,000.
vehicleFloor.important: This is not a guaranteed resale price; severely damaged or well-kept vehicles can have much different market values.

vehicleMileage.title: Odometer mileage
vehicleMileage.meaning: Enter the total distance shown on the vehicle odometer in kilometres, not today's trip.
vehicleMileage.example: If the dashboard reads 45,600 km, enter 45600.
vehicleMileage.important: Mileage is stored for reference but does NOT affect the current depreciation calculation.

loanOverview.title: About recording loans
loanOverview.meaning: The loan tool tracks outstanding debt and estimates payoff. Cash loans deposit actual funds into your account; purchase installments do not.
loanOverview.example: For a 1,000,000 cash loan with up-front fees, record the net funds actually received separately from the contractual principal and fees.
loanOverview.important: Warning: projections assume declining-balance annual interest, while recorded payments reduce principal. Flat-rate installments, service fees, and prepaid charges may not match the provider schedule.

loanName.title: Loan name
loanName.meaning: Identify a particular loan contract or installment. Avoid lumping unrelated purchases together when they have different repayment schedules.
loanName.example: Kredivo – Phone, SPayLater – Shoes, or KrediFazz – November loan.
loanName.important: Unused credit limits are not outstanding debt; do not double-count the same purchase as an expense.

loanType.title: Loan type
loanType.meaning: Mortgage, Auto, Student and Personal are primarily display groups, not specialized repayment engines.
loanType.example: For Kredivo cash loans and paylater, Personal is the closest current type, but the amortization may not match.
loanType.important: KrediFazz cash loans, Kredivo purchase installments, SPayLater, and SPinjam are different products.

loanCurrency.title: Loan currency
loanCurrency.meaning: Choose the currency of the debt contract.
loanCurrency.example: For most Indonesian installment providers, choose IDR.

loanPrincipal.title: Original loan principal
loanPrincipal.meaning: The original amount borrowed or financed, not the credit limit, future payments including fees, or net proceeds after deductions.
loanPrincipal.example: If a 1,000,000 cash loan has 60,000 of upfront fees, the contractual principal may still be 1,000,000 while cash received is 940,000.
loanPrincipal.important: Distinguish principal from total scheduled future payments with interest and service fees.

loanBalance.title: Outstanding loan balance
loanBalance.meaning: The amount still owed on the balance date. The app stores debt as a negative account balance.
loanBalance.example: If the original principal was 1,000,000 and 750,000 remains, enter 750000.
loanBalance.important: Recorded repayments currently reduce principal. For installments containing fees or interest, reconcile to the lender's official balance.

loanAPR.title: Annual interest (APR)
loanAPR.meaning: The interest rate used by the app's declining-balance model. Do not equate flat monthly loan charges directly to APR.
loanAPR.example: A contract with 12% annual effective interest can use 12; 2.6% flat monthly is not simply an equivalent 31.2% APR.
loanAPR.important: Never enter 0% just because the rate is unknown. A zero-interest promotion may still charge administration or service fees.

loanTerm.title: Loan term
loanTerm.meaning: The number of months stated by the contract.
loanTerm.example: Six monthly installments means 6 months; a 15-year mortgage is 180 months.
loanTerm.important: Short paylater terms such as 1, 3, 6, 9, or 12 months can be typed directly even if the quick menu lists years.

loanStart.title: Loan start date
loanStart.meaning: The contractual disbursement or purchase date, not when you first entered the loan in Lajur..
loanStart.example: An installment purchase made on 10 November 2026 may start then even if the first payment is in December.
loanStart.important: This field does not itself record money received or correct the outstanding balance.

loanPlanned.title: Planned monthly payment
loanPlanned.meaning: The actual amount you intend to pay each month. It informs payoff estimates; it does not send a payment.
loanPlanned.example: If the lender bills 380,000 monthly, enter 380000 and verify the provider schedule.
loanPlanned.important: For flat fees, payments include interest and charges; Lajur.'s projection does not automatically separate these.

loanMinimum.title: Minimum required payment
loanMinimum.meaning: The minimum contractual payment to avoid missing obligations, which may differ from the usual installment.
loanMinimum.example: For a credit card it may differ from the total bill; for paylater use the amount shown on the actual schedule.
loanMinimum.important: The form's suggested payment uses standard amortization. Do not use it instead of the provider's bill.

loanPaymentDay.title: Repayment due date
loanPaymentDay.meaning: Day of month on which repayment is due.
loanPaymentDay.example: If due on the 15th, enter 15; a rolling 30-day contract may shift.
loanPaymentDay.important: Day 29–31 can fall on the final day of a shorter month. Use the official schedule.

loanLender.title: Lender / provider
loanLender.meaning: The institution actually financing or administering the loan, which may differ from the shopping platform.
loanLender.example: SPayLater financing may be from Commerce Finance; SPinjam is a separate provider. Check the contract.
loanLender.important: Do not assume all Shopee products are from the same lender.

loanReference.title: Contract reference
loanReference.meaning: An identifier that links bills and payments to the contract.
loanReference.example: Use a recognizable agreement or transaction ID from the provider.
loanReference.important: Do not save passwords, PINs, OTPs or full identity documents here.

loanBalanceDate.title: Balance effective date
loanBalanceDate.meaning: Date at which a corrected outstanding balance becomes valid.
loanBalanceDate.example: If official debt becomes 750,000 on 10 November, use that date when correcting it.
loanBalanceDate.important: Backdated edits can change historical charts.
